messages.text: Your refund proposal is for **R$ 159.90**. Please confirm the exact proposal using the button on the proposal card; a reply in chat won’t confirm it. Once confirmed, a staff member will review it.
The customer confirmed request prop-8eb7388f18a54037 and a staff member approved it, so it is ready to be paid.

The refund of **R$ 159.90** has been recorded. Your receipt number is **R-00000001**. In this demonstration, the receipt records it in the shop’s test ledger, not as a bank transfer, and the shop can’t provide a date for money to appear on a card (refund-policy/v2/payout).
Is an actual refund to my original payment method possible?

tool_calls.name: lookup_refund_policy
tool_calls.arguments: {"query":"whether refund is an actual bank/card transfer to original payment method, distinction of test ledger receipt and no date funds appear"}

messages.name: lookup_refund_policy
messages.content: {"ok": true, "sections": [{"citation": "refund-policy/v2/payment", "title": "Where the money goes", "text": "A refund is paid automatically only when the order has exactly one payment record and that record is valid (a known payment method and a positive amount), and only to that payment. Instalments of one payment are one payment record. When the order has several payment records, or its one record is not valid, a staff member takes the case. A refund can never be sent to another person, account or card: such a request is refused with this reason, and the refund can still go to the original payment if the customer accepts. A customer's statement that the original card was cancelled does not change where the refund goes; the card's issuer handles the credit, and the shop cannot promise where or when it appears."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v2/payout", "title": "When the money is paid", "text": "The shop pays a refund only when all of these hold: the order qualifies, the request was on time, the units were received back and not refunded before, the order has one valid payment, the customer confirmed, a staff member approved, and the proposal is still valid. The refund is complete only when the customer has a receipt; until then nothing is reported as refunded. In this demonstration a receipt records the refund in the shop's test ledger: it is not a bank transfer, and the shop gives no date for the money to appear on a card."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v2/approval", "title": "Confirmation and approval", "text": "Every refund needs two separate decisions: the customer confirms the exact proposal (items, quantities and amount) with the button on the proposal card, and a staff member approves it. A message in the chat confirms nothing. Until a proposal is paid, the customer can cancel it with the button on its card; a message in the chat does not cancel it either. Changing anything in a proposal needs a new proposal, a new confirmation and a new approval. A staff member cannot approve a refund that this policy does not allow, and a staff member who rejects a proposal gives the reason, which the customer is told."}], "note": "Cite a section by its citation ID, exactly as given."}

messages.text: The shop’s refund is recorded in its test ledger; it is not an actual bank transfer, and the shop can’t promise when money will appear on your card (refund-policy/v2/payout). The policy says refunds go only to the original payment method when the order’s payment record qualifies; it doesn’t establish that a separate transfer will occur (refund-policy/v2/payment).
Could you check whether my payment qualifies for a refund to the original payment method?
